newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - LatAm ADRs firm on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - LatAm ADRs firm on U.S. data.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) for Latin American companies were largely firmer on Friday as fears eased of higher U.S. interest rates.

"The Latin American stocks were awaiting (employment) data out of the Labor Department and are really just following the U.S.," a trader said. Wall Street stocks were boosted by a January employment report that showed a slight rise in hourly wages and lessened prospects for the Federal Reserve tightening interest rates.

ADRs in Latin American bellwether Telebras were up 7/8 to 89-1/4. The Brazilian state holding distanced itself from an announcement by the nation's communications minister that it would see a 1996 profit of $3.08 billion reais, saying the year's accounts had not been closed.
Telefonos de Mexico ADRs were unchanged at 37-1/4 after Smith Barney cut its rating to neutral from outperform.
Britain's Barclays Plc rose 1-3/4 to 76-1/2 on prospects that the bank would report increased yearly profits this month.
Reuters Holdings Plc fell 1-3/4 to 62-1/4 "on weakness out of London," a trader said. The international news and information group will report results on Tuesday.
Shares in Canadian mining company Campbell Resources were unchanged at 13/16 on heavy volume of 1.1 million shares. The company was among the most active foreign shares.
A source said the volume was caused by a single block trade. Further details were not immediately available.
Advancers led decliners by 273 to 212 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 41 million shares in early afternoon.
